panels.figure_caption: Typical hookworm infection was confirmed through microscopic examination of the worm captured via endoscopy.
in_text_mentions: To investigate further, gastroscopy and colonoscopy were performed. While colonoscopy yielded no significant findings, gastroscopy identified living worms in the pyloric ring, antrum, and duodenum, along with areas of active bleeding (Figure 1). The worms were removed using biopsy forceps and were morphologically identified as Ancylostoma duodenale, a finding confirmed by microscopic examination (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: The histopathologic image shows a low-power (100x) view of Ancylostoma species exhibiting an intact nematode cross-section and internal structures, confirming the diagnosis of hookworm infection as detailed in the case report.
panels.attribution_text: Philip et al. Hookworms in the Stomach: Concurrent Gastric Ancylostomiasis and Gastric Adenocarcinoma Video Case Report.. ACG case reports journal 2026. doi:10.14309/crj.0000000000002313. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Low-power (×100 magnification) histopathologic image of Ancylostoma species demonstrating an intact nematode cross-section with preserved cuticle and internal structures (hematoxylin and eosin stain).
in_text_mentions: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed a large, ulcerated lesion with a fibrinous base and friable margins along the lesser curvature and incisura (Video 1, Figure 1), confirmed as moderately differentiated gastric adenocarcinoma with a desmoplastic stroma (Figure 2). Translucent, S-shaped worms were also seen attached to the gastric mucosa (Video 1, Figure 3) and duodenum, confirmed as Ancylostoma species on histology (Figure 4).
